purpose: Bounded search for a cash-only strategy that meaningfully beats a US index fund, with rules fixed from published research before testing. User asked to loop until something is found; this protocol keeps the loop honest.
constraints: No borrowing, shorts, leveraged funds or derivatives. Long-only, fully cash-funded. Rules taken from the original publication with its headline parameters; no tuning after seeing results.
trial_budget: At most 12 candidates in total. Every registered candidate counts, pass or fail, including those added in later batches. Later batches are registered here before they are run.
validation_window: Out-of-sample = first month after the end of the original paper's data sample, to 2026-08 (Kenneth French data end). Must be at least 14 years. Earlier data is reported but is in-sample for the idea.
benchmark: US market total return (French Mkt-RF + RF). ETF checks also report SPY, GLD and a monthly-rebalanced 50/50 SPY/GLD mix.

pass_rules_all_required.P1: Net annualized (CAGR) excess over the market >= 3.0 percentage points in the out-of-sample window.
pass_rules_all_required.P2: Newey-West (12 lags) t-statistic of monthly net excess >= 2.64 out of sample (one-sided 5% with a Bonferroni split over 12 trials).
pass_rules_all_required.P3: Net CAGR excess >= 0 over 2007-01 to 2026-08, so the effect is not dead in the recent regime.
pass_rules_all_required.P4: Maximum month-end drawdown no more than 10 percentage points deeper than the market's over the out-of-sample window.
pass_rules_all_required.P5: Where a liquid ETF implementation exists, its CAGR over its own live history (from first full month, 0.10% per traded side) is at least SPY's. Where none exists the candidate cannot be proposed for implementation.

outcome: Passing all five makes a candidate a proposal for a frozen prospective test and later Aurel3 tracking. It does not authorize trading or any live change.

C1_industry_momentum.source: Moskowitz & Grinblatt (1999), Do Industries Explain Momentum? Journal of Finance. Data sample ends 1995-07.
C1_industry_momentum.rule: 12 Fama-French value-weighted industries. At each month end rank by total return over the past 6 months; hold the top 3 equally weighted next month.
C1_industry_momentum.costs: Turnover x 0.10% per side plus 0.15%/yr fund fees (sector-ETF style).
C1_industry_momentum.etf: Same rule on the 9 original SPDR sector ETFs (XLB XLE XLF XLI XLK XLP XLU XLV XLY) from 1999.

C2_small_value.source: Fama & French (1992), The Cross-Section of Expected Stock Returns. Sample ends 1990-12.
C2_small_value.rule: Hold French SMALL HiBM (value-weighted small-cap, high book-to-market) portfolio.

C3_big_profitable.source: Novy-Marx (2013), The Other Side of Value: The Gross Profitability Premium. Sample ends 2010-12.
C3_big_profitable.rule: Hold French BIG HiOP (large-cap, high operating profitability).
C3_big_profitable.etf: QUAL (MSCI USA Quality; related but not identical).

C4_big_conservative_investment.source: Titman, Wei & Xie (2004), Capital Investments and Stock Returns. Sample ends 1996-12.
C4_big_conservative_investment.rule: Hold French BIG LoINV (large-cap, low asset growth).
C4_big_conservative_investment.etf: None liquid and matching; cannot pass P5.

C5_halloween.source: Bouman & Jacobsen (2002), The Halloween Indicator, American Economic Review. Sample ends 1998-08.
C5_halloween.rule: Hold the market November-April, T-bills May-October.
C5_halloween.costs: Two switches a year, 0.10% per side.

C6_global_dual_momentum.source: Antonacci (2012/2014), Risk Premia Harvesting Through Dual Momentum. Sample ends 2011-12.
C6_global_dual_momentum.rule: Monthly: if US market 12-month return > T-bill 12-month return, hold whichever of US or developed ex-US equities had the higher 12-month return; otherwise hold T-bills (aggregate bonds in the ETF version).

batch_1_result: 0 of 6 passed (results committed with batch 2 registration). ETF check fixed to use each ETF's own live history for P5; gold and 50/50 mix reported from GLD's start.

batch_2.registered_after: Seeing batch 1 results. Chosen for the largest documented long-only premia not yet tested; one budget slot is held back.

C7_value_momentum_blend.source: Asness, Moskowitz & Pedersen (2013), Value and Momentum Everywhere, Journal of Finance. Sample ends 2011-07.
C7_value_momentum_blend.rule: 50% French BIG HiBM + 50% BIG HiPRIOR, rebalanced monthly.
C7_value_momentum_blend.costs: 1.25%/yr drag (momentum turnover on half the portfolio, value on the other half).

C8_small_cap_momentum.source: Jegadeesh & Titman (1993), Returns to Buying Winners and Selling Losers. Sample ends 1989-12.
C8_small_cap_momentum.rule: Hold French SMALL HiPRIOR (small-cap, top 30% by months t-12 to t-2).
C8_small_cap_momentum.etf: XSMO (Invesco S&P SmallCap Momentum; earlier index history differs, approximate).

C9_net_repurchasers.source: Pontiff & Woodgate (2008), Share Issuance and Cross-sectional Returns, Journal of Finance. Sample ends 2003-12.
C9_net_repurchasers.rule: Hold French value-weighted portfolio of firms with negative net share issuance ('< 0' column).

C10_market_trend_filter.source: Faber (2007), A Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation. Sample ends 2005-12 (equity sleeve only, US market).
C10_market_trend_filter.rule: Hold the US market when its month-end total-return index is above its 10-month average, else T-bills; signal at month end, trade next month.
C10_market_trend_filter.etf: SPY / BIL with the same rule (BIL from 2007; T-bill rate before).

C11_small_value_momentum_blend.source: Asness, Moskowitz & Pedersen (2013), applied to small caps. Sample ends 2011-07.
C11_small_value_momentum_blend.rule: 50% SMALL HiBM + 50% SMALL HiPRIOR, rebalanced monthly.
